subsystems.name: Sensing array
subsystems.role: picks up electrical activity from the scalp and muscles.
parts: EMG electrodes over forearm or jaw
optional fNIRS optodes for blood-oxygen signals

subsystems.name: Analog front-end
subsystems.role: amplifies and digitises microvolt-level signals without drowning them in noise.

subsystems.name: Signal conditioning
subsystems.role: removes artefacts and extracts usable features.

subsystems.name: Decoder
parts: optional small language model for context-aware command mapping

subsystems.name: Headband and electrodes
subsystems.role: keeps sensors in stable contact with the skin for hours.
parts: conductive gel or dry contact pads

subsystems.name: Radio and power
subsystems.role: sends data to a phone, computer or headset and runs for a day.
parts: Bluetooth Low Energy or Wi-Fi radio

subsystems.name: Host integration
subsystems.role: makes the decoded intent act like a keyboard, mouse or gamepad.

buildSteps.title: Design the headband
buildSteps.detail: Place electrodes over motor-cortex regions and EMG sensors where they will not shift during head movement.

buildSteps.title: Make the electrodes
buildSteps.detail: Fabricate dry conductive pads or hydrogel electrodes that maintain stable impedance on skin.

buildSteps.title: Build the electronics
buildSteps.detail: Assemble a low-noise analog front-end, microcontroller and radio on a flexible printed circuit board.

buildSteps.title: Write firmware
buildSteps.detail: Sample at a few hundred hertz per channel, filter, and stream data with low latency.

buildSteps.title: Collect training data
buildSteps.detail: Record the user imagining or performing specific movements while the intended command is labelled.

buildSteps.title: Train the decoder
buildSteps.detail: Fit a model to map signal patterns to commands; use data from many users, then fine-tune per person.

buildSteps.title: Calibrate for the user
buildSteps.detail: Run a short session to adapt to the individual's anatomy and signal patterns, and correct for drift.

buildSteps.title: Integrate with the host
buildSteps.detail: Expose the decoder output through standard input APIs so it can control a cursor, select items or type.

buildSteps.title: Test and iterate
buildSteps.detail: Measure accuracy, false activations and comfort over long sessions, then refine hardware and model.

prerequisites.why: they avoid gel but still struggle with stable contact through hair.
wearable EEG and EMG devices already need tiny, quiet amplifiers.
deep learning has improved motor-imagery classification, but accuracy remains limited outside the lab.
small neural networks can run locally without sending raw brain data to the cloud.
a wearable can already emulate a keyboard or pointer once intent is decoded.

pathway.milestone: commercial EEG and EMG wearables for simple control, focus tracking and rehabilitation games
pathway.unlocks: comfortable sensors and basic intent detection.

pathway.milestone: reliable motor-intent decoding for cursor control and short text entry
pathway.unlocks: hands-free use of ordinary desktop and mobile software.

pathway.milestone: multimodal headbands combining EEG, EMG and fNIRS
pathway.unlocks: higher bandwidth and fewer false triggers in noisy environments.
everyday neural control without a training session or a technician.
